resources.convention: The backend lives entirely in the backend/ directory of the repository. Java 21, Spring Boot 3.5.x (parent org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-parent), built with Maven (the `mvn` command; use ./mvnw if the repository already has the Maven Wrapper). The root package is the package of the @SpringBootApplication class already in the code; keep that groupId, artifactId and package. Split packages by layer: controller (@RestController, only maps HTTP <-> DTO), service (@Service, business logic, @Transactional), repository (Spring Data JPA), domain (@Entity), dto (Java records for request/response). A controller never calls a repository directly. Do not change any file outside backend/.

resources.convention: Test with JUnit 5 + spring-boot-starter-test. Controller tests use @SpringBootTest + @AutoConfigureMockMvc (or @WebMvcTest when testing only the web layer). Every endpoint has at least one test for the success path and one for an error (400/404). Tests must not depend on the real database file of the dev environment - use a temporary SQLite file: @DynamicPropertySource points spring.datasource.url at a file in JUnit's temp directory (`@TempDir static Path tempDir`), as the repository's skeleton test already does. Do not delete database files in a test and do not change src/test/resources/junit-platform.properties: that file turns off JUnit's temp directory cleanup, because Windows will not delete a SQLite file while the Spring context still has it open. `mvn -B test` in backend/ must pass without the network except to download dependencies.

resources.convention: The database is SQLite through the JDBC driver org.xerial:sqlite-jdbc, with the Hibernate dialect org.hibernate.community.dialect.SQLiteDialect (dependency org.hibernate.orm:hibernate-community-dialects, version managed by Spring Boot). The default URL is already in the skeleton's application.properties (jdbc:sqlite:./data/<name>.db; the data/ directory must be in .gitignore). Keep spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate - migrations manage the schema, Hibernate must not generate it. Store time columns as ISO-8601 UTC TEXT; map Instant with an AttributeConverter<Instant, String> because the SQLite JDBC driver does not convert Instant on its own. Do not use H2, PostgreSQL or MySQL.

resources.convention: The schema is managed with Flyway (flyway-core) in backend/src/main/resources/db/migration, named V<n>__<description>.sql. Column types: id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, strings TEXT, booleans INTEGER (0/1), time TEXT ISO-8601. A committed migration is never edited; a schema change is always a new V<n+1> file. SQLite allows one writer at a time: keep transactions short, never hold a long transaction open across a request.
